Control Objective: Ensure sensitive attributes and their close proxies do not drive Beacon outputs
Control Description: Before build freeze Credit Analytics documents every model feature and its source; confirms age; name; language and marital status are excluded; and tests FSA and employer for proxy strength against census-based demographics. Any retained high-proxy feature needs a documented AI Governance Committee decision
Evidence Produced: Feature register with sign-off; proxy analysis report; committee minutes for any retained feature
Testing Frequency: Annual and at each material model change
Test Procedure: Internal Audit compares the production feature list to the approved register and confirms every retained high-proxy feature has a dated committee decision
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.11; MAP 2.3 | ISO 42001 Annex A.7 | EU AI Act Art. 10(2) (benchmark) | Canadian human rights legislation (Legal to confirm grounds by province)

Control Objective: Detect differential outcomes before deployment when demographic data is not collected
Control Description: Credit Analytics runs pre-deployment fairness testing using three proxy methods: geographic analysis against census data; name-based analysis; and synthetic matched pairs that differ in one proxy attribute only. Model Risk Management challenges the results. Results are compared with thresholds set by the AI Governance Committee (OI-07). Methods and their limits are documented and results are never used to decide individual applications. Legal confirms the methods are lawful first (OI-09)
Evidence Produced: Fairness test report with methods; data; results and limitations; Model Risk Management challenge memo; Legal confirmation
Testing Frequency: Before pilot and before each rollout expansion
Test Procedure: Internal Audit re-runs the matched-pair test on a sample of files and reproduces the reported gap within a stated tolerance; confirms thresholds match committee minutes
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.11; MEASURE 2.1 | ISO 42001 Annex A.5 and A.6 | EU AI Act Art. 10(2); Art. 9 (benchmark)

Control Objective: Detect emerging fairness drift in live outcomes
Control Description: An automated report compares Standard Review; Enhanced Review and Recommend Decline rates for proxy-inferred groups against a reference group; weekly in pilot and monthly after. The 0.80 ratio is an investigation trigger only and not a legal standard. Each breach is logged and routed to the AI Governance Office with a disposition within 5 business days
Evidence Produced: Monthly fairness report; breach log with dispositions
Test Procedure: Internal Audit recomputes the ratios for one month from raw outcome data and confirms every breach has a logged disposition within 5 business days
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.11; MEASURE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 (operation and monitoring) | EU AI Act Art. 72 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 monitoring expectations (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Provide independent challenge of soundness; performance and fairness before use
Control Description: Model Risk Management (second line) independently validates Beacon before pilot: conceptual soundness; out-of-time and segment performance; the reject inference approach; reason code behaviour; and the fairness results from CTL-02. Findings are rated and every high-rated finding must be closed before the approval gate
Evidence Produced: Validation report; findings log; closure evidence; approval gate minutes
Testing Frequency: Before pilot; annually; and on material change
Test Procedure: Internal Audit confirms the validator is independent of the developers and that every high-rated finding has closure evidence dated before the gate decision
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.3; MEASURE 2.5; MEASURE 2.11 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 (verification and validation) | EU AI Act Art. 9; Art. 15 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 validation and independent challenge (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Confirm real-world performance as repayment outcomes mature
Control Description: A quarterly backtest compares scores with realized repayment outcomes overall and by segment against the validation baseline and agreed tolerances. Outcomes lag 6 to 12 months so CTL-12 provides interim evidence. Breaches follow the escalation trigger in the register
Evidence Produced: Quarterly backtest report with segment results and tolerance comparison
Test Procedure: Internal Audit re-performs one quarterly backtest from source data and agrees the results to the report; confirms any breach was escalated
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.3; MEASURE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 | EU AI Act Art. 15; Art. 72 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 ongoing monitoring (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Keep adjudicator judgement independent on the highest-risk path
Control Description: The Workbench requires a written rationale on every Recommend Decline file whether the adjudicator follows or overrides it and the rationale must cite file facts and not the score. The Human Oversight Framework (Artifact 6) lists mandatory override and escalation triggers such as a conflict between the summary and the source documents; the file cannot be completed until the adjudicator records a decision or escalates to a team lead
Evidence Produced: Workbench configuration record; rationale capture logs; escalation log
Test Procedure: Internal Audit tries to complete five test Recommend Decline files without a rationale and confirms the Workbench blocks completion; samples 25 live rationales for quality
Framework Mapping: NIST MAP 3.5; GOVERN 3.2 | ISO 42001 Annex A.9 | EU AI Act Art. 14(4) (benchmark)

Control Objective: Measure whether adjudicators reach sound decisions without seeing the recommendation
Control Description: A random sample of files (5 percent proposed as a starting rate) goes to blind re-review: the adjudicator decides before Beacon's recommendation is displayed. Blind decisions are compared with Beacon and with a senior reviewer panel and results feed CTL-08 and CTL-09
Evidence Produced: Sample selection log; blind versus assisted comparison; senior panel results
Test Procedure: Internal Audit re-draws the sample using the documented method and confirms selection was random and blind decisions were recorded before display
Framework Mapping: NIST MAP 3.5; MEASURE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.9 | EU AI Act Art. 14(4)(b) (benchmark)

Control Description: Workbench data feeds a report of concordance with Recommend Decline; override rate and median review time by adjudicator and team; weekly in pilot and monthly after. Team concordance above 90 percent in a month or an override rate below 3 percent triggers an AI Governance Office review and a tier reassessment. Both thresholds are starting values to calibrate against the pilot baseline
Evidence Produced: Concordance and override reports; escalation records; tier reassessment memos
Test Procedure: Internal Audit recomputes one month of concordance from Workbench logs and confirms each breach produced a reassessment record
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.4; MANAGE 4.1 | ISO 42001 Cl. 9.1 and Annex A.9 | EU AI Act Art. 14; Art. 26 (benchmark)

Control Objective: Ensure adjudicators understand model limits and keep independent skill
Control Description: Before getting Workbench access adjudicators complete training on Beacon's limits; automation bias and the mandatory override triggers. New adjudicators assess files before viewing Beacon during onboarding and everyone passes an annual manual-only competency check. Access is granted only after completion
Evidence Produced: Training content; completion records; competency check results; access provisioning records
Test Procedure: Internal Audit compares the Workbench user list with training completion records and confirms no user lacks a current completion
Framework Mapping: NIST GOVERN 2.2; MAP 3.5 | ISO 42001 Cl. 7.2 and 7.3 | EU AI Act Art. 4; Art. 14(4) (benchmark)
